name: Expired Juice
flavorText: Died five or more times. The juice has definitely turned.
description: Somewhere between your fourth and fifth death, the Spirit Healer learned your name. You're a regular now. The tank is tired, the healer is tired, and whatever juice was in you has long since separated into sediment and cloudy water. Consider a flask. Consider a new talent build. Consider a cinnamon roll break.

name: Gravity's Favorite
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. The floor missed you.
description: The rest of the party had a run. You had a series of unplanned naps. Whether it was swirlies, ground pools, or just vibes, the floor kept pulling you in like you owed it money. Every GCD you pressed was a preamble to a death animation.

name: Designated Juice Drop
flavorText: You personally delivered more than half of the party's deaths.
description: If the party's deaths were a pie chart, you'd be most of the pie. Every time the group wiped there was a better-than-even chance your name was on the death recap. The other four made it look easy. You made it look expensive.

name: Silent Partner
flavorText: Zero interrupts while the rest of the party did all the kicking.
description: Every other keybind on your bar was pressed. Every other keybind. Meanwhile the rest of the party played whack-a-mole with every cast bar that popped up. Your kick button is officially filing for neglect. Possibly considering a restraining order.

name: Kick Commissioner
flavorText: Most interrupts in the party. The boot.
description: Every caster. Every chain-heal. Every ability with a cast bar. Your kick button is worn smooth. Somewhere a Deadly Boss Mods warning is feeling redundant.

name: 2% Pulp
flavorText: Second from the bottom. The forgettable middle of the meter.
description: Not bad enough to shame. Not good enough to praise. You are the beige cardigan of the party — the slot everyone mentally skips past when reading Details. Somewhere in Azeroth a bard is NOT writing a song about you.

name: Out-Juiced by the Driver
flavorText: A DPS out-damaged by the tank. The tank drove AND pressed the gas.
description: The tank's job is to hold aggro and not die. They did those things. They also outdamaged you. You had one responsibility in this run and it wasn't staying alive. Maybe try a different keybind. Or a different class.

name: Juice Thief
flavorText: A DPS out-damaged by the healer. Somebody check the rotation.
description: The healer kept the party alive AND put out more damage than you. They were doing two jobs. You were doing about half of one. Consider: what is a DPS, really? Who is the DPS in this group? Introspect. Growth awaits.

name: Tourist
flavorText: Dealt less than 10% of the party's damage. Just here for the sights.
description: You queued up for the dungeon tour, took a few photos at the landmarks, and let the rest of the group handle logistics. A beautiful experience for you. A character-building experience for everyone else.

name: Flat Soda
flavorText: No burst, no fizz. Your peak barely cleared your active average.
description: Other DPS have cooldowns, burst windows, and Bloodlust moments. You have a line. A flat, consistent, beverage-left-open-overnight line. Whatever 'pop CDs' means to you, it apparently means 'keep doing the same thing.' A steady effort, but the boss never feels threatened.

name: One Trick Spigot
flavorText: One big pop and then crickets.
description: Bloodlust hit, every cooldown lit up, Details sang, and then… you were done. The rest of the run you were essentially a very expensive autoattack. A quarter of your entire contribution happened in five seconds. Impressive in isolation; concerning in context.

name: Almost Taste It
flavorText: Another DPS was just barely ahead. You could taste it.
description: You and another DPS traded blows for the entire run. Your Details bars were practically kissing. Five hundred DPS separated an average run from a bragging-rights screenshot. Maybe next time skip the trinket swap. Maybe this time, enjoy how close it was.

name: Fresh-Pressed
flavorText: Top damage in the party. Certified squeezy.
description: Nobody pressed their abilities like you pressed yours. You were the top of the meter, the reason the boss fell when it did, and the reason the tank felt safe pulling bigger. Someone in Discord is going to link your logs unprompted. Don't be modest.

name: Juice Overflow
flavorText: Over 40% of the party's damage came from you. A one-person carry.
description: The other four players wanted a calm dungeon. You wanted a highlight reel. You accounted for nearly half of everything damaged in the key, which is either a carry or an accusation of the other DPS. Both interpretations are correct.

name: Concentrate
flavorText: The biggest burst spike in the party. Flash-pressed.
description: There is a reason people dread standing near you in Bloodlust. A full cooldown cycle from you looks like a PvP crit screenshot. Of every DPS in this party, you had the most extreme gap between your best 5-second window and your normal combat output — a true burst specialist.

name: Juice Leak
flavorText: Four or more party deaths happened on your watch.
description: Either the DPS keep standing in the bad or you let them. Either way, the death recap had four chances to have someone else's name on it and the Spirit Healer learned the whole roster. That's not a leak — that's a burst pipe.

name: Overflow Pour
flavorText: More than half of your healing was overheal. Wasted casts.
description: You had the biggest heals, the fanciest cooldowns, and a trinket proc to rival a raid boss. And half of it went into people who were already at full HP. Every wasted crit was a GCD you could have spent on damage, mana, or just not clicking at all. The juice flowed freely — right past them.

name: Dispel Denial
flavorText: Zero dispels while the rest of the group cleansed. Juice hoarder.
description: Somewhere out there a DPS had a debuff with your name on it. A curse, maybe. Magic, perhaps. A disease, who knows. You definitely didn't. Your cleanse button went the entire dungeon without seeing daylight.

name: The Juicer
flavorText: A healer who out-damaged a DPS. Multitasker of the month.
description: Healing is hard. Damage is hard. Doing both while the tank pretends to understand threat is very hard. Yet here you are, on the DPS meter, above an actual DPS. Someone's M+ review this week is going to be a painful conversation.

name: Steady Tap
flavorText: You survived the whole run. Job one, done.
description: When the healer goes down, everyone's day gets complicated — the tank panics, the DPS spam 'BR?' in party chat, and the whole key wobbles sideways. You didn't. You stayed at the tap, keeping the juice flowing, watching the tank take hits with a calm 'I've got you.'

name: Juice Dispensary
flavorText: Most dispels in the party. Juice's purification wing.
description: Curses, magics, diseases — whatever the dungeon threw at the group, you scrubbed it off before anyone else noticed. The rest of the party barely knew their debuffs existed. Somewhere a tooltip is thanking you by name.

name: Keeper of the Pour
flavorText: Zero party deaths on your watch. Every cup stayed full.
description: The DPS stood in some bad things. The tank forgot some defensives. And somehow none of it mattered, because you were a healing machine. Every dip in health was a blip. Every close call a story nobody else noticed. Not one Spirit Healer visit, on any member, the entire run.

name: Juiced Yourself Dry
flavorText: Self-healing overheal. Panic defensives at full HP.
description: Every tank has the oh-crap button. You pressed it at 99% HP. Repeatedly. Your Death Strikes, Ignore Pains, Shield Blocks, whatever you main — a huge chunk of them went into a health bar that didn't need them. The juice filled the cup, then kept pouring onto the table.

name: Free Juice for the Boss
flavorText: A tank with zero interrupts. Every cast got a free pour.
description: You hold aggro. You take hits. You pull big. Respected. You also have a kick, a stun, and probably a silence macro somewhere. Every single one of them sat on the bar while the raid leader typed 'KICK' in party chat for the seventh time.

name: Crash Test Dummy
flavorText: The tank led the party in deaths. The crumple zone worked.
description: The healer was trying. The healer was trying really hard. Your defensive rotation looked less like a rotation and more like a vibe. You led the party not in DPS, not in kicks, but in a stat no tank wants to lead — the death count.

name: Steel Press
flavorText: Tanked the whole run without dying. Cold-pressed.
description: Every big pull, every dangerous swirly, every tank buster — you ate them and asked for seconds. The healer barely had to use their panic cooldown. A tank who doesn't die is a tank who lets the rest of the group be comfortable. Thank you for your service.

name: Pasteurized
flavorText: Zero deaths for the entire run. Clean batch.
description: No Spirit Healer visits. No corpse runs. No 'sorry sorry sorry' in party chat. Every mechanic got respected, every avoidable was avoided. Rare. Beautiful. The juice came out clear.

name: Triple Concentrate
flavorText: A +3 upgrade. Maximum juice compression.
description: Beating the timer is one thing. Beating it by 40% is a statement. Every pull felt planned, every route felt right, every DPS pressed every button. Somewhere in the back end of the database, this run's row is glowing.

name: Vintage
flavorText: A new personal record for this dungeon or affix combo.
description: Personal best, stamped, bottled, labeled, and placed on the top shelf. Every future run on this key is going to have to beat this one. Good luck, future you.

name: Spilled Juice
flavorText: Depleted. Whatever juice was in there is on the floor now.
description: You ran out of time. You ran out of cooldowns. You ran out of healer mana. The timer turned red and what remained was a cup of regret. On the bright side, the key is one level lower and full of character-building opportunities.

name: Juice Rinds
flavorText: Depleted by a wide margin. Nothing left but the peel.
description: This wasn't a close call or a tragic loss. This was a full dungeon's worth of everything going wrong. The timer was gone well before the last boss. Brush yourself off — there's always next reset.

name: Over-Squeezed
flavorText: Deaths cost the party more than a minute of timer.
description: Every death adds five seconds to the clock. You found the ceiling of that formula. More than sixty seconds of your timer just went to the Spirit Healer's coffee fund. The run wasn't impossible; it was simply survived.

name: Group Juice Cleanse
flavorText: Every single member of the party died at least once.
description: Not a single player escaped. Tank down. Healer down. DPS down, sometimes twice. At some point in this run everyone saw the Spirit Healer's welcome screen. A bonding experience. A humbling one.

name: Cold-Pressed
flavorText: Top damage in the party. Slow extraction, maximum yield.
description: Other DPS pressed buttons. You pressed the right buttons. The boss bar moved like it was scared of your rotation, and Details lit up green every time you opened a cooldown. Whatever you're drinking before keys, keep drinking it.

name: Top Shelf
flavorText: Highest-output DPS in the run. Premium pour.
description: Top of the meter, top of the recap, top of the conversation in party chat that nobody actually has the courage to start. Keep that gear logged. Someone's about to ask for it.

name: Liquid Gold
flavorText: Topped the damage meter. Bottled and sealed.
description: Some DPS deal damage. You deal in damage. Every cooldown you popped felt like watching a Bloodlust commercial. The boss ate every GCD you served and asked for the recipe. Top of every meter that mattered tonight.

name: The Squeeze
flavorText: Top damage. Wrung out every percent.
description: You found the gap, you closed the gap, you topped the gap. Every trash pack got the same treatment: full pull, full output, full smile. Whoever was second on the meter is currently rewatching their replay.

name: Pulp Royalty
flavorText: Wore the citrus crown for this run. Long live the king.
description: Every DPS dreams of being top of the meter. You did it without making it weird. Just clean execution, clean numbers, and a quiet 'well played' in chat from someone whose pride is currently rebuilding.

name: Hand-Picked
flavorText: Top damage. Quality you can taste.
description: Whatever the pull, whatever the affix, whatever the lag — you found a button to press and you pressed it correctly. Topped the meter without flexing about it. The kind of DPS people actually want to invite back.

name: Pulped
flavorText: Led the party in deaths. Crushed flat.
description: You weren't a player tonight, you were a smoothie ingredient. Whatever was hitting the floor kept finding new ways to hit you specifically. The death recap reads like your character's autobiography.

name: Bruised Fruit
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. Showing the dents.
description: Picked, dropped, picked up, dropped again. Every party has someone who eats every avoidable mechanic and tonight that someone was wearing your name. The healer would like a moment to themselves, please.

name: Floor Vintage
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. Aged horizontally.
description: A truly fine run lying down, with notes of swirly, ground pool, and what was that boss doing. Distinct character. Pairs well with regret. The cellar of M+ has a special shelf for runs like yours.

name: Recycle Bin Regular
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. Frequent visitor.
description: The Spirit Healer recognizes you on sight at this point. Birthday discount probably available. Whatever the mechanic, you found a way to be in front of it and behind in the recovery.

name: Crushed Citrus
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. Pulp on the floor.
description: Look, juicing is messy work and tonight you provided most of the mess. The avoidables avoided everyone except you, like they had a list. The boss's mechanic tooltip should add an asterisk: you, specifically.

name: Designated Driver
flavorText: Most deaths in the party. Carrying the wipe.
description: The other four players took turns having a normal run. You took every turn. The death recap is essentially a one-name credits roll. A historic effort in the wrong direction.

name: Pulp Friction
flavorText: Depleted. The plot got messy.
description: Two pulls in, the run fell apart in a way that felt cinematic. By the third boss the timer was already a memory. Brush off the popcorn, queue the next one. Some keys are like sequels — best forgotten.

name: Closing Time
flavorText: Timer ran out. Lights up.
description: Last pull, last cooldown, last hope, last 30 seconds, all gone. The bar staff is sweeping up. You can stay until the boss falls but the timer doesn't care anymore.

name: Out of Juice
flavorText: Depleted. Tap ran dry.
description: Cooldowns dry, mana dry, patience dry. Sometimes a run is just a wide net of small things and tonight every fish got away. Reset, regroup, requeue.

name: Past the Best-By
flavorText: Depleted past the timer. Slightly off.
description: The ingredients were fine. The recipe wasn't. Somewhere between the second pull and the third boss, this run quietly went past its best-before date. Still drinkable. Just bitter.

name: Curdled
flavorText: Depleted. Something turned partway through.
description: Started smooth. Got chunky. Couldn't recover. Every party knows the moment a run goes from we got this to we have to try now. You found that exact moment and stared at it.

name: Stale Pour
flavorText: Depleted. No fizz, no finish.
description: Every CD landed five seconds too late. Every pull got two more pulls than planned. Every break was a beat too long. You went through the motions; the timer noticed.

name: Glass Pitcher
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. Fragile pour.
description: The healer was working their full kit. The DPS were respecting your cooldowns. The boss apparently was not. You shattered like the dungeon had it personally rehearsed against you, and the recap is mostly tank-shaped.

name: Bottom of the Bottle
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. Drained to the dregs.
description: Every defensive used. Every cooldown traded. Every health bar emptied. There was always one more swing than there was tank, and the dungeon knew it. Whatever was in your bottle, it ran out before the last boss did.

name: Cracked Carafe
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. Hairline turned full break.
description: One bad pull and a defensive on cooldown, and suddenly the whole structure went. Healer mana sailed past 0% trying to plug the cracks. Some runs you tank; some runs you crumble. Tonight was the latter.

name: Lid Off
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. Pressure unsealed.
description: When the tank goes, everything behind the tank goes too. Mobs scattered. Healer scrambled. DPS stopped DPSing. Every death after the first was just gravity finishing what your defensive rotation started.

name: Decanter Down
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. The good vessel hit the floor.
description: Tanks dying at all is a moment. Tanks dying most is a story. Whoever was healing tonight is currently writing a memoir, and the chapter on you has citations. The recap will live in screenshots.

name: Spilled the Set
flavorText: Tank led the party in deaths. Brought the rest of the tray.
description: When the lead glass goes over, the whole tray follows. Every wipe in the recap had your name at or near the top, and a depressing number of corpses fanned out behind you like a service of tragic dishware.

name: The Fountain
flavorText: Zero deaths as healer. Never stopped flowing.
description: Tanks took hits, DPS took dumb hits, bosses took swings — and through all of it, the green bar at the bottom of the screen stayed green. You weren't a healer tonight, you were public infrastructure. Citizens of M+ thank you.

name: Endless Refill
flavorText: Healer survived the run. Kept the cup topped.
description: Mana never bottomed, defensives never failed, your own health never dipped past comfortable. While four other people were learning what a Spirit Healer's UI looks like, you were busy doing your job. Cleanly. Repeatedly.

name: The Source
flavorText: Zero deaths as healer. Origin held firm.
description: Everything good in this run came back to you. Topped HP after a tank-buster? You. Cleanse on the dispel mob? You. Survival across every chaotic pull? Also you. The party drinks from the source and the source did not run dry.

name: Self-Sealing
flavorText: Healer never died. Patched themselves and everyone else.
description: Damage came in. Damage went out. None of it got past you. Whatever the DPS did to themselves, you fixed; whatever the boss did to you, you fixed faster. A solo masterclass in nobody-dies-on-my-watch.

name: Last Pour Standing
flavorText: Zero deaths as healer through the whole run. Held to the final swing.
description: The DPS were on their second corpse run. The tank was sweating through the last 5%. You — calm, mana-stable, still pouring out heals like it was a Tuesday morning. Every clutch screenshot in the recap has your name at the top of the kept-alive list.

name: Unspillable
flavorText: Zero deaths as healer. Sealed lid, stable hands.
description: Some healers fold under one bad mechanic. You had a full run's worth of bad mechanics aimed at you and didn't fold once. Maybe the run was clean, maybe it was a horror show — the party doesn't always know. The healer always does.

name: Spoiled Rotten
flavorText: Died five or more times. Whatever was in the cup turned.
description: The fridge light is on. The juice has been in there a while. Nobody's drinking what you're serving. Every time you came back something was a little less appetizing about the run, and by the fifth death the party had stopped looking.

name: Compost Pile
flavorText: Died five or more times. Returned to the soil.
description: Some players nourish a run. Others nourish whatever's growing under it. The graveyard learned your spawn point. The Spirit Healer started leaving the door unlocked. Eventually the party stopped reading the death recap because it was just one name on loop.

name: Fermented
flavorText: Died five or more times. Past juice. Into something else.
description: Each death bubbled the run a little more sideways. By death three you were technically a different beverage. By death five, the dungeon was a science experiment and you were the variable. Bold flavor profile. Not for everyone.

name: Returnable Bottle
flavorText: Died five or more times. Kept getting redeemed.
description: Every five minutes the party paid a deposit and got you back from the depot. The healer's mana bar opened a tab. The DPS stopped expecting cleanup. You came in dented, came back dented, came back denteder.

name: Six-Pack Short
flavorText: Died five or more times. Counted them on one hand and then some.
description: The pack came home incomplete. Five empties in the recap, plus whatever sixth one nobody wants to talk about. Some runs are about quantity. This was that.

name: Mass Spillage
flavorText: Died five or more times. Cleanup on aisle dungeon.
description: Five deaths is a lot. Six is a category. Seven plus is a federal disaster. Whoever's mopping the floor in this dungeon should bill the party. Specifically you. They'll find your details on the recap.

name: The Bouncer
flavorText: Most interrupts in the party. The list is the list.
description: Casters need cast bars. You don't recognize cast bars. Every cast bar that tried to get past you got the same answer, and the answer was a foot. The dungeon's casters filed a complaint. You filed it under your boot.

name: Bottle Cap
flavorText: Top interrupts. Sealed every cast.
description: Twist, lock, click — every cast bar got the same treatment. You closed the lid on more casters than the rest of the party combined. The boss tried to summon an add. You said no. The boss tried to heal. You said no harder.

name: Cancel Culture
flavorText: Top interrupts. No platform for casters.
description: Every cast had a chance. Every chance was revoked. By the second pull the casters were probably casting telepathically because their bars had stopped mattering. A masterclass in early-stage cast denial.

name: Hush Service
flavorText: Top interrupts. White-glove silence.
description: Smooth, professional, on-time, every cast. The boss never got a word in. The trash never finished a sentence. The most interrupts in the party and the rest didn't even come close — meanwhile the chat just had clean kills back to back.

name: Curfew
flavorText: Top interrupts. Every cast was past hours.
description: Every cast tried to start. Every cast was reminded it was past their bedtime. The dungeon's casters went home unfulfilled. The party kept moving because nothing got off cooldown long enough to matter.

name: Lid On
flavorText: Top interrupts. Closed every cup before it spilled.
description: Cast bars fill. You shut them. That's the whole job. You did it more than anyone, and the run reflected it — fewer surprises, fewer adds, fewer panic CDs. Every kick is a beverage that didn't spill onto the rug.

name: Triple-Distilled
flavorText: +3 upgrade. Refined down to the essence.
description: Anything inefficient got cut. Anything redundant got skipped. Anything dumb got punished. The route felt like it had been planned twice and executed once. Forty percent under par is a mood. The party found it.

name: Triple Shot
flavorText: +3 upgrade. Fully caffeinated.
description: Bloodlust on cooldown, every cooldown lined up, every interrupt landed. The party walked in tired and walked out vibrating. Nobody pulled small. Nobody healed conservatively. The timer? Cooked.

name: Lightning in a Bottle
flavorText: +3 upgrade. The kind of run people screenshot.
description: Every player's best version showed up tonight. Every cooldown landed in the right window. Every pull was just a little bigger than the last. Forty percent under par on a key, that's a moment — clip it before someone forgets.

name: Speed Pour
flavorText: +3 upgrade. Out before the cup could settle.
description: Whoever the timer was set for, it wasn't the party. Forty percent under par means the dungeon barely had time to introduce itself. Everyone earned the +3 and probably a stamina debuff for sprinting through it.

name: Fast-Pressed
flavorText: +3 upgrade. Cold-pressed has a sibling, and it's faster.
description: The slow-extraction crowd will tell you good juice takes time. The +3 crowd will tell you good juice takes everyone pressing every button. You took the second school. The keystone agreed.

name: Trifecta
flavorText: +3 upgrade. Three for three.
description: Every chest, every threshold, every count. The keystone needed three boxes ticked and the party ticked them with time to spare. Walk-in numbers like that get logged and people ask questions. The questions are usually who carried.

name: House Record
flavorText: New personal best. The cellar has a new top shelf.
description: Every previous run on this key just got moved down a notch. The leaderboard inside your own profile got rewritten. Future-you is going to look at tonight's row and decide whether to chase it or pretend it didn't happen.

name: Limited Edition
flavorText: New PB. Special label.
description: Nobody else has run exactly tonight's run. Same affixes, same comp, same outcome — never again. You bottled lightning, slapped a serial number on it, and slid it onto the back wall of the cellar. Don't drink it. Just look at it sometimes.

name: Reserve Stock
flavorText: New personal best on this key. Locked in the back.
description: A new entry in the personal cellar. Aged, labeled, tagged for special occasions. Every key you run on this dungeon from now on is going to have to clear this number first. Good luck, future you.

name: First Bottle
flavorText: New PB. The first one off the line.
description: First time the dungeon got pressed this hard. First time the affix combo bent this far. First time the timer looked like that. Bottle it; you don't get many firsts.

name: Bottling Day
flavorText: New personal best. Worth keeping.
description: Some runs are just runs. This one earned a label, a date, a slot on the rack. Whatever the party did right tonight, it was right enough that the personal best line moved. The next run on this key is going to feel a lot less casual.

name: Cellar Reserve
flavorText: New personal best. Top shelf.
description: Best of every previous run on this dungeon, distilled into tonight's row. Whatever you were chasing — the affix combo, the dungeon time, the streak — the chase ended with a screenshot worth saving. The cellar door just got a deadbolt.

name: Tank Down
flavorText: Tank died at least once. Even the strongest cup spills sometimes.
description: Maybe it was a missed defensive. Maybe it was a chained tank-buster. Maybe it was the affix you keep forgetting about. The point is: the tank went down, and the dungeon paused to let everyone notice. Healers everywhere felt that one.

name: Cracked Lid
flavorText: Tank died this run. Hairline showed through.
description: The seal held for most of the dungeon. Then it didn't. One pull went a little too long, one button hit cooldown a little too late, and the bar emptied. Every tank has these runs. The recap just won't let you forget yours.

name: Defensive Lapse
flavorText: Tank died at least once. The rotation slipped.
description: Every defensive on a CD, every CD on a timer, every timer slightly out of sync — that's all it takes. You ate the swing the rotation should've covered. Tighten it up next pull. The party's still rooting for you.

name: First Pour Down
flavorText: Tank died this run. The first vessel hit the floor.
description: The party drinks from the tank. When the tank goes, the cup goes. Tonight your cup hit the floor at least once and the rest of the party watched it bounce. The shape of the run changes after a tank death. Your shape too.

name: Cup Tipped
flavorText: Tank died. Tipped further than recoverable.
description: Tilt past 90 degrees and it's no longer a tip, it's a spill. Whatever angle your defensive rotation was at tonight, the dungeon found the exact tip-over point and pushed. Recoverable, but not while horizontal.

name: Dropped the Tray
flavorText: Tank died this run. The tray came with you.
description: When a tank goes, mobs follow. Aggro tables reset. The healer plays goalie. Every tank death sends a small tremor through the rest of the run, and tonight the party felt yours. Bring the tray back next pull.

name: Bottled at the Buzzer
flavorText: Timed with under 30 seconds remaining. Sealed at the last possible second.
description: The party hit the last cooldown, hit the last button, hit the last percent — and the timer hit zero a heartbeat later. A run like this is 50% skill, 50% one perfect pull at the end, 50% nobody breathing for the final 30 seconds.

name: Last Drop
flavorText: Timed with under 30 seconds. The cup got the last pour just in time.
description: Whatever was in the tank when the last boss died, it was the last bit. No headroom. No reroute. The clock ticked into single digits and the party crossed the line on fumes. Earned.

name: Photo Finish
flavorText: Timed by less than 30 seconds. Both runners crossed the line at once.
description: The timer doesn't take screenshots, but it could've. A run that lives at the boundary between timed and depleted, and nobody's quite sure what mattered most until the loot pops.

name: Razor Pour
flavorText: Timed with under 30 seconds. Margins thinner than the glass.
description: The kind of timer where if any one player had stuttered, the whole thing depletes. Every kick mattered. Every cooldown mattered. Every second mattered. And the run came in on the right side of the math.

name: Final Squeeze
flavorText: Timed with under 10 seconds. Wrung the dungeon dry.
description: Five seconds left. Ten. Pick a number, it doesn't matter — the party squeezed every last drop out of every last cooldown and the dungeon barely had time to react. The kind of run that becomes a Discord clip.

name: Buzzer Beater
flavorText: Timed with under 30 seconds. Crossed under the bell.
description: Some runs end with time to spare. Some end like this — heart rate spiked, last-stand defensives all on cooldown, party emoting nervously. The bell rang. You crossed first. That's all that matters in the recap.

name: Personal Mute Button
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts alone. Kept the casters on silent.
description: Four party members had a dungeon. You had a full-time job of cancel-keys. Every cast bar that lit up, you doused. The other interrupters got a vacation. The casters got nothing.

name: One-Person Door
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts. Solo bouncer.
description: The kick rotation was supposed to be shared. You took it as a one-line role description. By the second pull the party stopped pre-targeting because they'd just watch you handle every cast like it was personal.

name: Solo Bouncer
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts. Worked the velvet rope alone.
description: No coordination needed. No backup needed. Whoever was on the cast bar, you were already mid-kick. The casters in this dungeon are now telling stories about you to younger casters. The stories are not flattering.

name: The Whole Cap Run
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts. Single source of silence.
description: Twist, lock, click — every cap of every bottle, you did the work. The rest of the party just kept walking. By the end of the run you had memorized the dungeon's cast list and the dungeon had memorized your boot.

name: The Mute Squad of One
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts. The full kick department, in one player.
description: Whatever party comp you were running, the kick rotation was a solo. The other four didn't need to learn the cast list. You were the cast list, and the bar was always at zero. A historic effort in keeping the room quiet.

name: Single Source Silence
flavorText: Did 75%+ of party interrupts. The hush came from one place.
description: One cast bar. One kick. Repeat. Forever. Every time something tried to get off, the answer came from the same direction at the same moment. The dungeon's casters started checking your position before they even cast.

name: Eye of the Storm
flavorText: Zero deaths while the party racked up 4 or more. Calm in the middle.
description: The dungeon was on fire. The recap looks like a horror movie. And in the middle of all of it, you didn't fall once. While the rest of the party was learning what the Spirit Healer's UI looks like, you were just playing.

name: Untouched Bottle
flavorText: Zero deaths while the party fell. The cup never hit the floor.
description: Four party members took at least one swing they couldn't recover from. You didn't. Maybe you were paying more attention. Maybe you were luckier. Either way, the death recap had four spots for your name and they're all empty.

name: Dry Above the Flood
flavorText: Zero deaths during a high-death run. Stayed above water.
description: While the rest of the party was figuring out how the spirit healer queue works, you were figuring out the next pull. Clean record on a dirty run. The kind of player every group secretly hopes shows up.

name: Last Cup Standing
flavorText: Zero deaths while the party racked up 4 or more. Held when nothing else did.
description: Some runs are just chaos and the death recap looks like a casualty list. Yours wasn't on it. You stood through the whole thing — every wipe, every rebuild, every GG message that didn't come — and finished untouched. Memorable.

name: Held the Glass
flavorText: Zero deaths in a chaotic run. Hand never shook.
description: The party went sideways. You didn't. Whatever mechanics took down four other players, you read, dodged, or just outright ignored. It's not always the loudest performance — but the recap notices when one name is missing from the death column.

name: Stable Stem
flavorText: Zero deaths in a high-death run. Roots held.
description: Wind's blowing, leaves are everywhere, half the garden is on the ground — and the one stem you're attached to didn't snap. Sometimes a run is about output, sometimes it's about not contributing to the wreckage. Tonight you nailed the second.

name: The Perfect Pour
flavorText: Praise across the board, no roasts, zero deaths.
description: Top of the meter, a kick or two, every cup full and not a single death. The kind of run people screenshot before logging out. The juice came out clear, the recap is poetry, and the dungeon is going to need a minute.

name: Clean Sheet
flavorText: Every column on your row says yes. Every column.
description: Damage, kicks, deaths, dispels — pick a column, you nailed it. No roast on your card, multiple praises lit up. The kind of player every group secretly hopes shows up. Bottle this one.

name: Distilled to Perfect
flavorText: Every dimension positive. No flaws to fault.
description: Every measurement we took came back green. Damage was up, kicks were on, deaths were zero, party survived because of you. Whatever you're doing this run, keep doing it. The juice has reached its final form.

name: Complete Disaster
flavorText: Three roasts, zero praise. A full set.
description: Every dimension we measured found a way to disappoint. Damage low, deaths high, kicks missing — pick a roast, you've earned it. The recap is going to need its own folder. Tomorrow's a new key.

name: The Unhappy Meal
flavorText: Three roasts, no praise. Combo deal of regret.
description: You ordered the everything-wrong set and the dungeon delivered. Wrong damage, wrong kicks, wrong deaths — every box on the recap got the bad checkmark. A historic effort in the wrong direction.

name: Poured Down the Drain
flavorText: Three roasts. Whatever was in the cup is gone now.
description: Every column lit up red. Whatever skill ceiling existed for this run, you went the other way. Every roast on the card connects to a different recap moment. Brush it off — keys reset eventually.

name: Sweet and Sour
flavorText: At least one praise AND at least one roast. Both at once.
description: Topped the meter and died five times. Most kicks and lowest damage. The recap reads like two different runs, both with your name on them. A polarizing performance — Discord will have opinions.

name: Chunky Smoothie
flavorText: Praise and roast in the same blender.
description: Some of it was great. Some of it was lumpy. The blender ran but the consistency is something you'd ask the bartender about. Mostly delicious. Mostly. The party will remember the praise OR the roast — depends on who you ask.

name: Two-Sided Label
flavorText: Praise on one side, roast on the other.
description: The bottle's front says one thing, the back says another. Front: 'Top of the meter.' Back: 'Died five times.' Both true. Both your work. Both featured prominently in the recap.

name: Triple Threat
flavorText: Top damage, biggest share, biggest burst. The complete DPS set.
description: You didn't just top the meter. You did 40%+ of the party damage AND had the biggest peak burst window in the run. Three different dimensions of damage dominance, all yours. People are now using you as the benchmark.

name: The Full Concentrate
flavorText: Topped damage, carried damage, biggest burst — a one-DPS show.
description: Top of the meter. Forty percent of party damage. Largest burst spike. There is no DPS dimension you didn't dominate. The other DPS are filing complaints with HR. The boss is filing complaints with the dungeon.

name: Single Origin
flavorText: All three damage praises. One DPS, every dimension.
description: The whole damage story this run came from one player. Top of meter, dominant share, biggest spike. The recap might as well just have your character's portrait taking up the whole panel. Bottle it. Frame it. Logs are public.

name: Anchor Overboard
flavorText: Three roasts on a depleted run. The boat went down with you on it.
description: Three different roasts on your card AND the timer didn't make it. Whatever sank this run had your fingerprints on it. The other four players will ABSOLUTELY remember. So will the recap.

name: The Weak Link
flavorText: Three roasts on a depleted key. Chain found its weakest point.
description: Every party has the player carrying the run. This run, your party didn't have one — they had you, going the other direction. Three roasts, depleted key. The recap is going to be a teaching moment in someone's Discord.

name: Sediment at the Bottom
flavorText: Three roasts on a depleted run. Settled to the bottom of the cup.
description: Whatever was supposed to flow through this run got stuck. Three roasts deep, timer gone, and the dungeon noticed. Some runs are bad luck. Some runs are bad reads. This was both, and the recap doesn't differentiate.

name: Held Up My End
flavorText: Two praises on a depleted run. You did your job.
description: The timer ran out, but the recap on YOUR card looks great. Top damage, big kicks, kept the cup full — none of it was enough this time. Sometimes you get the run you deserve. Sometimes the team gets the run they didn't.

name: Good in a Bad Run
flavorText: Multiple praises on a depleted key. A bright spot.
description: The dungeon won. Your individual play didn't lose. Multiple praises on your card, even though the timer didn't cooperate. Take the small win. Tomorrow's key is a fresh start.

name: Ace in the Hole
flavorText: Two praises on a depleted run. The card the party didn't draw.
description: Whatever the team needed tonight, you brought half of it. Multiple praises in the recap, on a key that didn't survive. The party had a wing-man. The wing-man could only do so much.

name: The Dream Team
flavorText: Every player got praise. Nobody got roasted. Vanishingly rare.
description: All five players earned at least one praise. Zero roasts on anyone. The kind of run that doesn't happen most weeks. Every cup stayed full. Every measurement landed in the green. The recap is a postcard.

name: The Perfect Batch
flavorText: Praise across all five players, zero roasts. Bottled.
description: Pour from any cup tonight and it tastes the same — perfect. Five players, multiple praises distributed evenly, no roasts anywhere. A party-wide masterclass. Save the screenshot; runs like this aren't on the schedule.

name: Clean Glassware
flavorText: Every player praised, none roasted. Spotless party run.
description: Five clean cups on the rack. Five sets of praise on the recap. Zero roasts to file. The run earned a separate folder in someone's logs because they're going to be linking it for weeks.

name: Everyone's a Critic
flavorText: Every player earned a roast. The whole table is bitter.
description: Pour from any cup tonight, it's lukewarm. Every single player has at least one roast on their card. Everyone contributed to the wreckage. The recap is just five small disasters stacked into a tall one.

name: The Whole Cup Spilled
flavorText: Every player got at least one roast. Zero clean records.
description: The recap looks like a five-way tie for last place. Every column has at least one red mark. Bonding experience: yes. Run worth bragging about: no. Brush each other off — every party has nights like this.

name: Five Strikes No Balls
flavorText: Every player roasted. The whole batting order missed.
description: Five players. Five roasts (or more). The recap is a strike-zone diagram with every pitch outside it. Some runs the team plays well. Some runs the dungeon plays better. Tonight the dungeon won by a wide margin.

name: Pure Mid
flavorText: Almost no achievements fired. The most average run in history.
description: Nobody topped anything. Nobody bottomed anything. Nobody died too much, kicked too much, or stood out at all. The recap could be five different runs and you couldn't tell. A genuinely forgettable, technically-fine outcome.

name: The Unflavored Run
flavorText: Almost no achievements fired. No notes worth tasting.
description: Pour the run into a cup, sniff it, look puzzled. Nothing extreme, nothing notable. Five players had a perfectly mid time. The recap is a single shrug emoji. A category of run that exists but rarely warrants a screenshot.

name: Library Voice
flavorText: Quiet run. Nothing exceptional in either direction.
description: Whisper, pull, kill, repeat. Nobody did anything wrong enough to roast. Nobody did anything right enough to praise. The dungeon was vanquished politely and everyone went home. A small badge for a small run.

name: The Full Pour
flavorText: 10+ positives party-wide. Every cup overflowed.
description: Ten or more praise badges fired across the run. The whole party nailed it — at every position, in every dimension. The recap is a wall of green. Whatever clicked tonight, schedule another night just like it.

name: Juice Flooding
flavorText: 10+ positives party-wide. The juice came out everywhere.
description: Damage, kicks, dispels, deaths-not-happening — pick a praise, it fired tonight. Ten or more across the party. The kind of run where every player's screenshot looks like a highlight reel. Pure flow state, group edition.

name: Festival of Praise
flavorText: 10+ positives across the party. Everyone's getting confetti.
description: The recap looks like a parade. Every dimension we measured fired green for someone. Tonight the party didn't have a weakness, the dungeon didn't have a counter, and the screenshots are going in the cellar with a label.
